import pandas as pd


def run(inputs: dict) -> dict:
    df = inputs["payments"].copy()

    valid_currencies = {"USD", "EUR", "GBP"}

    # Rule masks evaluated in order, each conditioned on NOT having matched
    # an earlier rule (first-failing-rule semantics).
    r1 = df["amount"].isna()

    r2 = (~r1) & (df["amount"] <= 0)

    # SQL-style NOT IN: NULL currency makes the comparison unknown (not TRUE),
    # so a null currency does not trigger R3; it falls through to R4.
    r3 = (~r1) & (~r2) & df["currency"].notna() & (~df["currency"].isin(valid_currencies))

    r4 = (~r1) & (~r2) & (~r3) & df["country"].isna()

    reject_mask = r1 | r2 | r3 | r4

    reason = pd.Series(pd.NA, index=df.index, dtype="object")
    reason[r1] = "AMT_NULL"
    reason[r2] = "AMT_NONPOS"
    reason[r3] = "CCY_INVALID"
    reason[r4] = "CTRY_NULL"

    rejects = df[reject_mask].copy()
    rejects["reason_code"] = reason[reject_mask]

    clean = df[~reject_mask].copy()
    clean["amount"] = clean["amount"].round(2)

    clean = clean.reset_index(drop=True)
    rejects = rejects.reset_index(drop=True)

    return {
        "payments_clean": clean,
        "payments_rejects": rejects,
    }
